title: Concept of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a society's categorization of its people into rankings of socioeconomic tiers based on factors such as wealth, income, race, education, and power. It is a persistent feature of human societies, determining access to resources, opportunities, and levels of privilege across different groups.

Modern sociological theory examines several models for understanding stratification, including caste systems (which are ascribed at birth) and class systems (which possess more mobility). Functionalist perspectives argue that stratification is necessary because differential rewards motivate individuals to perform roles deemed essential for societal function. Conversely, conflict theories suggest that stratification primarily serves to maintain the dominance of powerful groups over less privileged ones.
